name: Peach Blush
lede: Peach Blush is a warm reddish terracotta that Maerz and Paul dated to 1926, but our painting archive finds it concentrated centuries earlier, in South Asian painting.

sections.title: A 1926 fashion word
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary first records Peach Blush in 1926, on plate 5, swatch C11 [1]. Despite the fruit in its name, ColorHub's library files it under Browns, closer to terracotta and sienna than to any pink [1]. A peach's actual blush runs lighter and pinker than this swatch; the name describes the deeper shadow side of the fruit's skin, not its sunlit cheek [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[hyacinth-red]], [[ferruginous]] and [[polished-brown]], at 3.4, 
[[terracotta]], [[brick]] and [[red]] sit nearby in the same warm-earth family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Peach Blush in 584 of 23,781 paintings (2.46 percent), as photographed, mostly as a midtone or shadow color [2]. It is strongly concentrated in South Asian painting: 38 of 96 Kalighat paintings carry it, over 16 times the archive rate, and it runs almost as high in Pahari and Rajput work, and in paintings from Tibet, Nepal and India generally [2]. Pontormo and Amedeo Modigliani use it far more than their peers [2]. It keeps company with Vermilion, Sienna and Red more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
